sentences.text: Californosaurus is an extinct genus of marine reptile known from fossils found in California and Germany.
The animal possessed a long-snouted head that was small relative to its body, resembling primitive ichthyosaurs.
Its tail was sharply angled downward with a small vertical fluke, a trait shared with more advanced ichthyosaurs.
Fossil evidence suggests Californosaurus may have possessed a small dorsal fin.
The animal had between 45 and 50 vertebrae before the sacrum.
Its flipper bones were circular and widely spaced, creating a round appearance for the flippers.
Californosaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur reaching lengths of up to 3 meters.
John Campbell Merriam described the species in 1902 as Shastasaurus perrini, honoring discoverer James Perrin Smith.
Oscar Kuhn established the genus name Californosaurus in 1934 because the previous name Delphinosaurus was already used for a different animal.
Californosaurus fed on fish and other small marine animals.
Like other ichthyosaurs, it likely never left the water and gave birth in the sea.
Californosaurus belongs to the suborder Shastasauria.
It is considered one of the most basal true ichthyosaurs known.
Fossils are found in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic in California and the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic in Germany.
The genus lived during the Carnian age between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
